era: E2 1970-1979 low-loss fiber, heterostructure lasers, LiNbO3 integrated optics
event: Describes a new CVD-derived method: deposition inside a rotating, burner-heated fused-quartz tube; GeO2-doped fiber with loss minimum under 2 dB/km at 1.06 um; graded index.
dri: John B. MacChesney; P. B. O'Connor
dri_locator: p.1 byline (J. B. MacChesney first, P. B. O'Connor second of three authors)
orgs_printed: Bell Laboratories, Murray Hill, N.J.; Bell Laboratories, Crawford Hill, Holmdel, N.J.
key_figure_caption: Spectral attenuation (dB/km, log scale) versus wavelength, 500-1100 nm, of a step-index fiber with B2O3-GeO2-SiO2 core and borosilicate / silica cladding.
key_figure_reason: the measured loss spectrum behind the low-loss result
notes: Proc. IEEE, September 1974 (p.1 header), letter pp.1280-1281 = text.md pp.1-2; manuscript received 1974-05-20 (p.1). The cached pages also carry the end of a preceding TeO2 acousto-optic filter letter (p.1 left column, its Fig. 3) and the start of a different letter, Tasker and French, 'Low-Loss Optical Waveguides with Pure Fused SiO2 Cores' (p.2 right column); neither belongs to this paper. The paper does not use the words 'modified chemical vapor deposition' or 'MCVD' (it says 'a new method derived from CVD') and makes no 'first' claim. Fig. 1 fiber: 723 m long, core approximately 35 um, NA 0.235; loss minimum just under 2 dB/km at 1.06 um (p.1). Fig. 2: graded-index profile, maximum index difference 0.0165, alpha 1.6 (p.2). Byline J. B. MacChesney, P. B. O'Connor, H. M. Presby; the paper states no individual roles, so the papers.csv DRI is kept. Acknowledgment: F. V. DiMarcello drew the fibers; J. R. Simpson and P. D. Lazay made the spectral loss measurements; D. J. Freed mass spectrographic data (p.2). img_p01_1.png / img_p02_1.png are full-page scans; page_02.png used. Postal codes omitted. No component rows (optical fiber is not a component class).
